nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a game tree whose values lie in a bounded linear order with least element $\bot$ and greatest element $\top$. For either player $p$ to move, alpha-beta pruning run on $t$ for $p$ with the window $[\bot, \top]$ returns exactly the minimax value of $t$ for $p$.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta with the full window returns the minimax value

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a game tree with values in a bounded linear order, $p$ the player to move and $a, b$ values. If the minimax value $v$ of $t$ for $p$ satisfies $a < v < b$, then alpha-beta pruning run on $t$ for $p$ with the window $[a, b]$ returns exactly $v$.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta is exact inside the window

nodes.summary: Let $t$ be a game tree with values in a bounded linear order, $p$ the player to move and $a < b$ values. If the minimax value of $t$ for $p$ is at most $a$, then alpha-beta pruning run on $t$ for $p$ with the window $[a, b]$ returns a value at most $a$.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta fails low when the minimax value is at most the lower bound

nodes.summary: For all values $a, b$ in a linear order and every list $ts$ of game trees, the value returned by the alpha-beta scan of $ts$ for the minimizer with lower bound $a$ and upper bound $b$ is at most $b$.
nodes.title: The minimizer's alpha-beta scan stays at or below its upper bound

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be the player to move, $ts$ a list of game trees with values in a bounded linear order, and $a \le b$. Let $r$ be the value returned by the alpha-beta scan of $ts$ for $p$ with window $[a, b]$, and let $m$ be the best value for $p$ among $ts$: the maximum of the minimax values of the trees in $ts$ for the minimizer ($\bot$ if $ts$ is empty) when $p$ is the maximizer, and the minimum of their minimax values…
nodes.title: Correctness of the alpha-beta scan

nodes.summary: For either player $p$, all values $a, b$ in a linear order and every list $ts$ of game trees, the alpha-beta scan of $ts$ for $p$ with lower bound $a$ and upper bound $b$ evaluates at most as many leaves as the trees in $ts$ have in total, each leaf evaluation costing one unit.
nodes.title: Cost of the alpha-beta scan

nodes.summary: Given the player $p$ to move, values $a$ and $b$ in a linear order and a list of game trees (the children of a position), the scan runs alpha-beta pruning for the other player on the children in order, each time with the current bounds $a$ and $b$. The maximizer replaces $a$ by $\max(a, v)$, where $v$ is the child's returned value, and stops as soon as $b \le a$, returning the new $a$; if it never stops early it…
nodes.title: Alpha-beta scan of the children

nodes.summary: Alpha-beta is correct (Knuth and Moore 1975, Theorem 1): for `a ≤ b`, the result of alpha-beta agrees with the minimax value after clamping both to the window `[a, b]`.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta is correct

nodes.summary: For either player $p$ to move and all values $a, b$ in a linear order, alpha-beta pruning run on a game tree $t$ for $p$ with window $[a, b]$ evaluates at most as many leaves as $t$ has, each leaf evaluation costing one unit.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta never evaluates more leaves than the tree has

nodes.summary: For a player $p$ to move and values $a$ and $b$ in a linear order, alpha-beta pruning with window $[a, b]$ returns the value of a leaf at a cost of one unit (one leaf evaluation), and on an inner node runs the alpha-beta scan of its children for $p$ with window $[a, b]$.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta pruning

nodes.summary: A game tree with values in a type $\alpha$ is either a leaf, which carries a value in $\alpha$ (the value of a terminal position), or an inner node, which carries a finite list of game trees (the positions reachable in one move; the list may be empty). Game trees are built inductively, so every game tree is finite.
nodes.title: Game tree

nodes.summary: Let values lie in a linear order. For all values $a$ and $b$ and every finite list of game trees, the value returned by the alpha-beta scan of the list with the maximizer to move and window $[a, b]$ is at least $a$.
nodes.title: Lower bound for the maximizer's scan

nodes.summary: Let values lie in a bounded linear order, let $t$ be a game tree, let $p$ be a player, and let $a < b$. If the minimax value of $t$ with $p$ to move is at least $b$, then the value returned by alpha-beta pruning on $t$ with $p$ to move and window $[a, b]$ is at least $b$.
nodes.title: Alpha-beta at or above the top of the window

nodes.summary: The number of leaves of a finite list of game trees is the sum of the numbers of leaves of its members ($0$ for the empty list).
nodes.title: Number of leaves of a list of game trees

nodes.summary: The number of leaves of a game tree is defined recursively: a leaf counts $1$, and an inner node counts the total number of leaves of its children (so an inner node without children counts $0$).
nodes.title: Number of leaves

nodes.summary: Let values lie in a bounded linear order. For a player $p$ and a finite list of game trees, the value for $p$ is the best of their minimax values with the other player to move: for the maximizer, the maximum of these values, or $\bot$ if the list is empty; for the minimizer, the minimum of these values, or $\top$ if the list is empty.
nodes.title: Minimax value of a list of positions

nodes.summary: Let values lie in a bounded linear order. The minimax value of a game tree with player $p$ to move (the maximizer or the minimizer) is defined recursively: a leaf is worth the value it carries; an inner node is worth, for the maximizer, the maximum of the minimax values of its children with the minimizer to move, and for the minimizer, the minimum of the minimax values of its children with the maximizer to move. An…
nodes.title: Minimax value

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
